messages.subject: Multiple selection
parts:
Hi all,

I'm writing my first shiny app and I'm having some trouble with multiple selection.

When I select a single input (a letter between "a" and "e"), it works fine.
When I select more than one input, it returns the error: "EXPR must be a length 1 vector".

The desired output is a table with rows satisfying multiple criteria.

I paste some demo code, a simplified version of what I'm doing.

server.R
##################################################
library(shiny)

ddd <- data.frame(letters[1:5], 1:5)
colnames(ddd) <- c("c1","c2")
attach(ddd)
###
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
 
  datasetInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$variable,
    "a" = "a",
    "b" = "b",
    "c" = "c",
    "d" = "d",
    "e" = "e") 
    })
 
  output$ttt <- renderTable({
    crit <- datasetInput()
    head(subset(ddd, subset = lll %in% crit))
  })

  output$text <- renderText({
  input$variable
  })
                                      })
##################################################

ui.R
##################################################
library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
 
# title
headerPanel("My first app"),
 
###
  sidebarPanel(
   
    selectInput("variable", "Var:",
                choices = c("a","b","c","d","e"),
                multiple=T
                )
  ),

###
  mainPanel(
    textOutput(as.character("text")),
    tableOutput("ttt")
  )))
##################################################

Can someone give me the solution for this?
Thank you.
Best regards,
Carla

messages.author: b949e0841d7e094b
messages.subject: Re: Multiple selection
parts: Your second test has a problem here, I think

ddd <- data.frame(letters[1:5], 1:5)
> colnames(ddd) <- c("c1","c2")
> head(subset(ddd, subset = lll %in% crit))

Error in match(x, table, nomatch = 0L) : object 'lll' not found

in the console, make sure you object you return is a dataframe, then try again.

I also suggest you copy your ui.R and server.R into this:

https://gist.github.com/

After you copy the files, make a "public" gist, you copy-paste the url into your message.

then anyone can run it with 
library("shiny")
runGist("https://gist.github.com/...")

It's very quick and saves some copy-pasting.
